name: Bosch Dresden 300 mm wafer fab

parties.name: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action
parties.note: Bosch's factsheet says the fab received funding under the first IPCEI on microelectronics; no amount is given.

process_nodes.label: 65 nm
process_nodes.note: Bosch's 2023 factsheet gives structure widths down to 65 nm.

summary: Bosch's 300 mm wafer fab in Dresden, Germany, cost about EUR 1 billion, which Bosch called the biggest single investment in its more than 130-year history. It was inaugurated on 7 June 2021 and started production in July 2021, earlier than first planned, making ASICs and power semiconductors mainly for automotive and industrial uses; MEMS sensor production on 300 mm wafers was planned to start there in 2026. In July 2022 Bosch said it would spend EUR 250 million over the following year adding 3,000 square metres of cleanroom, and in November 2022 it said that expansion was under way.

metrics.note: To be spent over the year following the July 2022 announcement.
Existing cleanroom before the planned addition of about 3,000 square metres.
Workforce once construction is complete; about 250 people worked there at the opening.

milestones.note: Production for Bosch power tools; at the opening Bosch said this start was six months earlier than planned.
Planned start of chip production for automotive customers, stated at the opening.
The operator reported the cleanroom expansion under way in November 2022.

notes: The record is in scope for the fab's June 2021 opening and its 2022 cleanroom expansion. Bosch's August 2023 factsheet still lists the roughly 3,000 square metre addition as pending, and no source read for this record reports its completion, so the status remains partly operating as of that factsheet. In November 2026 Bosch said it had invested about EUR 3 billion in its Dresden and Reutlingen fabs in recent years, without splitting the amount.
